quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both words open the same way. Follow the rhythm to the end: where does the strongest beat land?
quests.explanation: That was "personal": the beat fell on the first syllable and the ending was weak. "Personnel" ends on a strong, clear /nel/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Listen for which syllable carries the beat: first or second.
quests.mouthPosition: Tap the beat on the strong syllable as you say the word.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The first vowel is the same. Listen to the consonant in the middle and how long the vowel lasts before it.
quests.explanation: Here, you heard "coding": the first vowel lingered slightly and the middle consonant stayed voiced. "Coating" has a crisper, voiceless closure.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Listen for the buzz across the consonant: /d/ has it, /t/ interrupts it.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the tip firm and the release short for /t/; make it looser for /d/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Focus on the strong first syllable. Wide or relaxed?
quests.explanation: You heard "ankle": the jaw dropped and the vowel was bright. "Uncle" is duller and more relaxed.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The tongue is forward and low for /æ/, but sits in the centre of the mouth for /ʌ/. To the ear, /æ/ sounds brighter and /ʌ/ sounds duller and flatter.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel the front of your tongue rise toward your teeth for /æ/; for /ʌ/ the tongue stays lazy and flat.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.textToSpeak: We stayed at a small hotel.
quests.hint: Listen for a short sound at the very end of the word.
quests.explanation: In the sentence, "stayed" finished with a quick /d/ after the vowel. "Stay" ends on the vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The past-tense -ed ending is pronounced as /t/ after voiceless sounds, /d/ after voiced sounds, and /ɪd/ after /t/ or /d/. Listen for the extra stop at the end.
quests.mouthPosition: Finish the base word, then touch the tongue tip to the ridge for a quick /t/ or /d/. Whisper it after voiceless sounds and voice it after voiced ones.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.textToSpeak: I saw the shoulder in the photo.
quests.hint: Both words start with a similar gliding vowel. Listen for hush or hiss at the start.
quests.explanation: "Shoulder" starts with a broad hush and ends softly. "Soldier" starts with a sharp hiss and has a /dʒ/ in the middle.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Compare the pitch of the friction: /ʃ/ is a deeper 'shh', /s/ is a bright 'sss'.
quests.mouthPosition: Say 'shh' as if asking for quiet, then smile and say 'sss'.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The first consonants are identical. Bright or dull vowel?
quests.explanation: It was "trucker": a short, dull vowel in the strong syllable. "Tracker" opens the jaw wide and sounds brighter.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Think 'wide and bright' for /æ/ against 'short and dull' for /ʌ/.
quests.mouthPosition: A big, wide mouth makes /æ/; a small, lazy mouth makes /ʌ/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same rhythm. Listen to the hiss at the start: sharp or soft?
quests.explanation: This time, "sinking" opened with a sharp, high hiss. "Thinking" has soft friction with the tongue at the teeth.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /θ/ is made by placing the tongue tip against or between the teeth and blowing air softly; /s/ is made with the tongue behind the teeth and a narrow groove, giving a sharper hiss.
quests.mouthPosition: For /θ/ let the tongue tip touch the edge of the upper teeth and blow gently. For /s/ pull the tongue back behind the teeth and narrow the air channel.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The two words differ only in the first vowel, and it is unstressed-ish. Tight or half-open?
quests.explanation: What you caught was "immigrant": the first vowel was short and tight. "Emigrant" opens a little more.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɪ/ is short and high-ish with the jaw nearly closed; /e/ is also short but the jaw opens further and the tongue lowers toward the middle.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ɪ/ keep the jaw almost shut with relaxed lips. For /e/ lower the jaw slightly so a fingertip could fit between the teeth.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The middle consonant is either smooth or begins with a stop.
quests.explanation: "Cashing" has a smooth hush in the middle with no stop. "Catching" starts with a stop and then a hush.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ʃ/ is a continuous fricative; /tʃ/ begins with a stop and then releases into friction, so it sounds abrupt at the start. Listen for a sudden beginning versus a smooth flow.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ʃ/ let the air flow steadily over the tongue. For /tʃ/ block the air with the tongue against the ridge, then release into a hush.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to what happens right after the first /ɡ/.
quests.explanation: That was "growing": the tongue curled back with no contact. "Glowing" touches the ridge with the tongue tip.
quests.vowelTensionRule: In a consonant cluster the /l/ or /r/ follows another consonant, so the difference is smaller. /l/ needs tongue contact at the ridge; /r/ needs a curled tongue tip and often shortens or devoices the first consonant slightly.
quests.mouthPosition: Say the first consonant, then for /l/ touch the tongue tip to the ridge, for /r/ curl it back without touching.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Does anything follow the /t/?
quests.explanation: In this phrase "hurts" ended with a hiss after the /t/. "Hurt" stops at the /t/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: A plural or third-person ending is a short fricative after the base word; missing it changes the meaning.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the tongue tip near the ridge and let the air flow at the end.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The consonant in the middle is either a hiss or a buzz.
quests.explanation: The word was "muscle": a clean hiss between the vowels. "Muzzle" buzzes.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Listen for a hiss (/s/) or a buzz (/z/) in the middle of the word.
quests.mouthPosition: Hold the same tongue position and switch the voice on and off.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.textToSpeak: We decided to adapt the plan.
quests.hint: The weak first syllable hides nothing. Listen to the strong vowel: bright or rounded?
quests.explanation: Here, "adapt" was bright and spread. "Adopt" is rounder and deeper.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /æ/ is a front vowel with lips slightly spread; /ɒ/ is a back vowel with the lips rounded a little. The tongue moves from front to back and the lip shape changes with it.
quests.mouthPosition: For /æ/ keep the tongue pushed forward and the lips slightly spread. For /ɒ/ pull the tongue back and round the lips a little.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.textToSpeak: That sentence is a bit wordy.
quests.hint: Same first syllable. What happens in the middle: a stop or a flow of air?
quests.explanation: You heard "wordy": the tongue tip stopped the air. "Worthy" lets voiced air keep flowing between the teeth.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /d/ blocks the air completely, /ð/ never does.
quests.mouthPosition: Look in a mirror: the tongue tip peeks out for /ð/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Does the word end with the hum, or does a stop follow it?
quests.explanation: In this phrase, "phoned" finished with a quick /d/ after the /n/. "Phone" stops on the hum.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The past form adds a short consonant to the end; the base form finishes with the earlier sound.
quests.mouthPosition: Add the tongue-tip closure at the end, even if you don't release it.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Focus on the vowel in the first, stressed syllable.
quests.explanation: What you caught was "bottle", a rounded, deep vowel. "Battle" has a wider, brighter vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Contrast the vowel colour: /æ/ sounds bright and sideways, /ɒ/ sounds deep and rounded.
quests.mouthPosition: Move your lips from a slight smile (/æ/) to a small round shape (/ɒ/) while the jaw stays open.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to the nasal in the middle. Tongue tip or back?
quests.explanation: In the sentence, "singer" used a deep nasal made with the back of the tongue. "Sinner" uses the tongue tip.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ŋ/ sounds deeper and lasts longer.
quests.mouthPosition: Do not add a /ɡ/ after /ŋ/ in these words.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Does the first sound stop the air or let it flow?
quests.explanation: That was "thanks": soft friction between the teeth. "Tanks" starts with a short burst.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The stop /t/ blocks the air completely before releasing it; /θ/ never stops the air.
quests.mouthPosition: The tongue is further forward for /θ/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The vowel is either a glide or a steady rounded one.
quests.explanation: This time, "chose" started relaxed and rounded off. "Choose" is steady and tightly rounded.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Listen for the glide: /əʊ/ opens a little before it closes. /uː/ stays closed and rounded throughout.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel your lips: still for /uː/, closing for /əʊ/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The middle consonant is either soft and voiced or crisp.
quests.explanation: The word was "bagging": the vowel was a bit longer and the middle consonant voiced. "Backing" is crisper.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The voiced /ɡ/ keeps the voice going across the closure.
quests.mouthPosition: Make the /k/ closure firmer and the /ɡ/ closure looser.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both are voiced in the middle. Soft friction between the teeth, or a sharper buzz?
quests.explanation: In this phrase "clothing" had soft friction with the tongue at the teeth. "Closing" had a sharper /z/ buzz.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ð/ and /z/ are both voiced fricatives, but /ð/ is made with the tongue at the teeth and sounds softer, while /z/ is made behind the teeth and sounds sharper.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ð/ put the tongue tip between the teeth and add voice. For /z/ pull it back behind the teeth into a narrow groove.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The vowel is identical. How does the middle consonant start?
quests.explanation: It was "watching": a stop and then a hush. "Washing" is a smooth hush.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /tʃ/ = /t/ + /ʃ/ in one movement; /ʃ/ has no stop.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel the tongue seal against the ridge before release for /tʃ/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen between the two vowels: is the friction breathy, or does the voice stay on?
quests.explanation: Here, "proving" buzzed softly between the vowels. "Proofing" had a breathy /f/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Between vowels, /f/ is a clear hiss and /v/ keeps the voice on through a softer, buzzier friction.
quests.mouthPosition: Lightly touch the lower lip to the upper teeth. For /v/ let the throat buzz; for /f/ blow air with no vibration.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Compare the strong syllable: a held, rounded vowel or a brief, open one?
quests.explanation: You heard "caller": a long, rounded vowel in the strong syllable. "Collar" is short and open.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɒ/ is short with the mouth open and lips slightly rounded; /ɔː/ is long, with the tongue raised further at the back and the lips more clearly rounded.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ɔː/ round the lips into a clear circle and let the tongue rise a little at the back. For /ɒ/ open the jaw and round the lips only slightly.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to the last sound of the word.
quests.explanation: In the sentence, "asked" ended with a stop, /t/, after the /k/. "Asks" ends with a hiss.
quests.vowelTensionRule: A short /t/ or /d/ closes the past-tense word, and it may be unreleased before a consonant.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the ending short and soft.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Contact or curl for the second sound?
quests.explanation: That was "playing": after the /p/, the tongue tip touched the ridge. "Praying" curls back.
quests.vowelTensionRule: After /k/, /ɡ/, /p/, /b/ or /f/, the /r/ pulls the lips and tongue back, while /l/ keeps the tongue tip forward.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the lips slightly rounded through the cluster for /r/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Is there a small puff of breath at the start?
quests.explanation: This time, "eating" began directly with the vowel. "Heating" starts with a soft /h/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /h/ is a breathy sound made in the throat, with the mouth already in the position of the following vowel; the alternative is a word that starts directly with the vowel. The cue is breath at the start.
quests.mouthPosition: Open the mouth in the vowel position and push out a gentle breath before voicing.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.textToSpeak: The waves are crashing on the rocks.
quests.hint: Listen to what follows the opening /k/.
quests.explanation: The word was "crashing": the tongue curled back. "Clashing" touches the ridge.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The tongue tip is forward and touching for /l/ and pulled back for /r/, even when it follows another consonant.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel the tongue tip move to the ridge for /l/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same first syllable. Buzz or hiss in the middle?
quests.explanation: In this phrase "losing" buzzed between the vowels. "Loosing" has a clean hiss.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Between vowels, /s/ is a clean hiss and /z/ keeps the voice buzzing; the preceding vowel is a little longer before /z/.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the tongue tip near the ridge behind your teeth. For /z/ vibrate the vocal folds; for /s/ let out only air.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.textToSpeak: I love riding in the morning.
quests.hint: Listen to the vowel length and the closure in the middle.
quests.explanation: It was "riding": a slightly longer vowel and a voiced tongue-tip closure. "Writing" is shorter and crisper.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Between vowels, /t/ is a crisp voiceless stop while /d/ remains voiced and slightly softer; the vowel before /d/ is also a little longer. (Here we are using careful British pronunciation, not the American 'flap'.)
quests.mouthPosition: Tap the tongue tip on the ridge behind the teeth. For /t/ make it crisp with a brief silence; for /d/ keep the voice buzzing.
